stemMd: An object is moved from Earth to a location with one sixth Earth's gravitational acceleration. What happens to its mass and weight?

options.label: D
options.textMd: Mass is unchanged; weight becomes one sixth.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Mass becomes one sixth; weight is unchanged.

explanationMd: Weight equals mg and therefore scales with local g. The object's mass remains the same, while its gravitational force becomes one sixth as large.

distractorRationale.b: Location does not multiply the object's mass.
distractorRationale.c: Weight depends on local gravitational acceleration.
distractorRationale.a: Mass is an intrinsic inertial property, not local gravitational force.
